label: Decompositions and Jacobians
notes: Chapter three turns matrices on the Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds into factored coordinates. We meet the singular value, polar, and QR decompositions, then compute the Jacobians that tell us how the invariant measure splits into latent roots and orientation. These factorizations are the engine of every distribution we sample later.

label: The Stiefel Manifold
notes: The Stiefel manifold collects matrices with orthonormal columns, the rectangular cousins of orthogonal matrices. Its invariant measure is the object we want to factor. Before differentiating anything, we fix notation: an n by k frame, its column space, and the rotations that act on the left and right without changing geometry.

label: Singular Value Decomposition
notes: Every real matrix factors as a left orthogonal frame, a diagonal of singular values, and a right rotation. Geometrically this is rotate, stretch along axes, rotate again. The singular values are the latent roots that will carry the radial part of any matrix-variate density, while the two orthogonal factors carry orientation.

label: Reading the SVD Geometrically
notes: The diagram traces the unit circle through three stages. The right rotation realigns it, the diagonal stretches it into an ellipse whose semi-axes are the singular values, and the left rotation places that ellipse in the output space. Holding this picture makes the later change-of-variables algebra feel inevitable rather than formal.

label: Polar Decomposition
notes: The polar decomposition writes a matrix as an orthogonal frame times a positive semidefinite symmetric factor, gluing two halves of the singular value decomposition. It separates a pure orientation from a pure stretch. On the Stiefel manifold this projection onto orthonormal columns is exactly how we map data back to the frame it most resembles.

label: QR and Gram-Schmidt
notes: Gram-Schmidt orthonormalizes columns one at a time, producing an orthonormal frame Q and an upper triangular R that records the projections discarded along the way. The triangular factor's positive diagonal makes the decomposition unique. This sequential view gives the cleanest path to a Jacobian, since each column adds one controllable layer.

label: Exterior Differential Forms
notes: To compute Jacobians on manifolds we use the wedge of differentials rather than a coordinate determinant. The exterior product is antisymmetric, so repeated differentials vanish and orientation is built in. The invariant measure on the Stiefel manifold is itself such a wedge of the entries of the skew matrix Q transpose dQ.

label: The Jacobian as Volume Scaling
notes: A Jacobian is the local factor by which a change of variables stretches volume. We picture a tiny coordinate cell mapped forward into a parallelepiped whose volume is the determinant times the original. On a manifold the same idea holds for the wedge of forms, letting us track how measure flows through a decomposition.

label: Jacobian of the SVD
notes: Differentiating the singular value decomposition and wedging the independent forms produces a Jacobian with a Vandermonde-like product of squared singular value differences. That factor is what couples the latent roots: it repels equal singular values and shapes every matrix-variate eigenvalue density built on this manifold. The orthogonal factors contribute their own invariant measures.

label: Factoring the Invariant Measure
notes: Putting the pieces together, the invariant measure on the Stiefel manifold splits into a latent-root part and an orientation part. The radial factor carries the singular values with their repulsion term; the orientation factor is the invariant measure on the orthogonal group. This separation is the whole reason the decompositions were worth computing.

label: Worked Check: 2x2 Frame
notes: We test the bookkeeping on a small frame. Parametrize a two-by-two case, compute the wedge of differentials by hand, and confirm the singular-value difference appears with the expected power. The notebook's diagnostic mirrors this: a finite invariant that stays stable as we vary the parameter, certifying the Jacobian was assembled correctly.

label: Summary and Outlook
notes: We factored matrices three ways, learned to differentiate those factorizations with exterior forms, and split the Stiefel measure into latent roots and orientation. The recurring repulsion product foreshadows the matrix-variate distributions of later chapters. Keep the rotate-stretch-rotate picture and the volume-scaling reading of the Jacobian close at hand.
